imageAlt: A sample check with numbered callouts.

hotspots.title: 1. Date
hotspots.text: The date the check is written (month/day/year).

hotspots.title: 2. Pay to the Order of
hotspots.text: Who the check is being paid to (a person or an organization).

hotspots.title: 3. Amount (Numbers)
hotspots.text: The payment amount written in numbers. This should match the written amount.

hotspots.title: 4. Amount (Words)
hotspots.text: The payment amount written out in words. If there is ever a mismatch, banks typically rely on the written amount.

hotspots.title: 5. Memo / For
hotspots.text: Optional note describing what the payment is for (rent, utilities, invoice #, etc.).

hotspots.title: 6. Signature
hotspots.text: The payer's signature. Without it, the check is usually not valid.

hotspots.title: 7. Your Information / Bank Information
hotspots.text: Typically includes the payer's name/address and/or bank name (format varies by check design).

hotspots.title: 8. Routing Number
hotspots.text: Identifies the bank. This is the first set of numbers in the MICR line at the bottom.

hotspots.title: 9. Account Number
hotspots.text: Identifies the specific bank account the money comes from (second set in the MICR line).

hotspots.title: 10. Check Number (MICR / Header)
hotspots.text: The check's ID number. Often appears at the top and again at the bottom (format varies).

hotspots.title: 11. Check Number (Top Corner)
hotspots.text: Another location where the check number may appear for easier reference.

hotspots.title: 12. MICR Line (Bottom Line)
hotspots.text: The machine-readable line that contains routing/account/check-number information for processing.
